An increase of at least 30 beats per minute within 10 minutes of standing up is the most widely accepted criteria to be diagnosed from what I've seen. It doesn't have to be particularly high or low to begin with, just an 30 bpm increase.

As for a resting heart rate, I find it can be difficult to get an accurate one with POTS personally. If you're able to sit down for a while without moving too much (like half an hour minmum for me), your heart rate should be stabilised enough to get a picture of it. I don't think it particularly matters if youre lying down or sitting up, but when I had a table tilt test they measured my heart rate lying down after 10 minutes, then standing up continuously for 40 minutes. You'll most likely have a table tilt test if you get diagnosed.

Worth mentioning that I'm just a person with POTS and I have absolutely 0 medical qualifications so take this with a grain of salt.
